Barratt Redrow Lowers Sales Outlook Despite Revenue Beat for Fiscal 2026
By Anthony O. Goriainoff
Barratt Redrow cut its sales guidance for the current fiscal year, but said that pretax profit rose in fiscal 2026 as revenue beat consensus.

The home builder on Wednesday said it now expects sales for fiscal 2027 between 17,500 and 17,900 units, down from a previous 17,700 to 18,200 units range. The company said this was due to continued delays in planning and the reduction in sales outlet openings to around 405 from previous expectations of around 415.
The company said that for the 52 weeks ended June 28, pretax profit was 363.5 million pounds ($489.9 million), compared with 273.7 million pounds the year before.
Revenue rose to 6.06 billion pounds from 5.58 billion pounds. Visible Alpha consensus for the metric stood at 5.99 billion pounds.
The company said the number of home sales rose 5% to 17,667. It had guided for total home sales of between 17,200 and 17,800 for fiscal 2026.
Net private reservations per outlet per week rose to 0.56 from 0.55. The rate from June 29 to  Sept. 6 was 0.62, compared with 0.55 last year.
The board declared a final dividend of 1.0 pence compared with 12.1 pence last year.

"Whilst the wider economic backdrop remains uncertain, we are focused on maximizing the strength of our three differentiated brands, maintaining our disciplined approach to costs and capital allocation," Chief Executive David Thomas said.
